commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Caitlyn
Add task tracking and list command
Implement mark command without extra classes
commitResults.messageBody: Track completion flags alongside task descriptions and add the mark command while keeping the chatbot's demure servant tone. Display completion markers in list output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement unmark command without extra classes
commitResults.messageBody: Add the inverse status operation using the existing parallel task and completion lists, preserving the requested list output and demure servant responses.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Task class for task state
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the parallel task and completion lists with a dedicated Task class that owns status changes and display formatting. Keep mark and unmark behavior in Caitlyn without introducing a separate TaskList class.

Provide a project-specific present-changes-visually skill based on the shared se-edu workflow. Include the self-contained split-view diff generator and Codex UI metadata so future work can be reviewed as an interactive HTML page.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ToDo deadline and event task types
Use conventional Todo task class name
Add fail-fast UI testing skill and plan
Handle invalid chatbot commands with exceptions
commitResults.messageBody: Add CaitlynException and route malformed inputs through a consistent error path. Reject empty ToDos and unknown commands with servant-style messages while preserving the existing task workflows, and extend the UI regression plan.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand UI tests for invalid input state safety
commitResults.messageBody: Interleave valid and invalid ToDo, Deadline, Event, mark, and unmark commands to verify rejected inputs do not change Caitlyn's internal task list or statuses.
Support deleting tasks by list number with collection-backed storage, removal confirmation, updated task counts, and regression coverage for valid and invalid delete commands.
Represent Todo, Deadline, and Event task kinds with TaskType values and centralize their display markers. This removes repeated task-type string literals while preserving the existing Caitlyn output.

Write the task list to data/duke.txt after successful additions, status changes, and deletions. Add polymorphic storage serialization for todo, deadline, and event tasks, and extend the UI test plan to cover the save path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load tasks from disk at startup
commitResults.messageBody: Restore todo, deadline, and event tasks from data/duke.txt with their completion statuses. Isolate UI cases in temporary directories and verify both saved-file output and startup loading.

Escape special task fields, write files atomically, validate malformed records, and roll back in-memory mutations when saving fails. Add regression coverage for corrupted data, special characters, and first-run startup without a data directory.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typed date and time support
commitResults.messageBody: Parse deadline and event values into LocalDateTime objects, format them for display, and persist canonical ISO values. Update the UI regression plan for date/time parsing and invalid-date handling.

Move Caitlyn's scanner input and console output into a dedicated Ui class, including the welcome message, separators, errors, task listings, and task confirmations. Keep command parsing, task mutation, and persistence in Caitlyn so this small refactoring preserves the existing behavior while establishing the first collaborator in the target design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command objects for application actions
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce an abstract Command type, a Parser, and concrete command classes for listing, adding, marking, unmarking, deleting, exiting, and rejecting unknown input. Move command-specific validation, task updates, persistence rollback, and UI responses out of Caitlyn so the main loop now parses and executes polymorphic commands while preserving all existing behavior.

Move all Java classes below the existing src/main/java source root and add package declarations so the project has a consistent named package. Update the UI test runner and setup documentation to use the packaged entry point.
Use Caitlyn as the Gradle application entry point and check the exit flag before waiting for more input. Add a regression case covering immediate termination.

Cover date parsing, task models, command parsing, and task-file persistence, including invalid inputs and escaping. Document the 50% high-value method coverage target so tests stay aligned after future code changes.
Rename the Shadow JAR to caitlyn.jar and document how to build, locate, and run it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Java code: Apply SE-EDU style conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Public APIs lack consistent Javadocs and several source files use
non-standard import ordering, line wrapping, and boolean names.

These inconsistencies make the code harder to review and maintain
against the project's adopted SE-EDU Java standard.

Add descriptive, punctuated Javadocs, order imports consistently, wrap
long diagnostics, and use has-prefixed boolean state names while
preserving runtime behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Java skill: Encode SE-EDU coding conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Java contributions need a reusable project-local reference for naming,
layout, statements, imports, variable scope, and Javadoc.

Without a local skill, future agents may apply the standard
inconsistently or rediscover the external guide.

Create the SE-EDU coding-standard skill with the authoritative link,
concise review checklist, and project-specific Java 25 verification
guidance.

and branch names.

A shared skill keeps future messages concise, imperative, and useful for
explaining WHAT changed and WHY.

Create the SE-EDU Git-standard skill with subject and body limits, scope
guidance, branch naming, and pre-commit review checks.

Allow users to search task descriptions by case-insensitive keyword while preserving original task numbers, with validation and regression coverage.

Document the command-dispatch and search-display responsibilities touched by the find feature. Keep the clarification limited to Javadoc so runtime behavior and existing UI assertions remain unchanged.
Integrate the JavaDoc and SE-EDU style cleanup so the main branch has consistent source documentation.
Integrate the project-local Java and Git standards so future contributions follow the documented conventions.

Integrate keyword search while retaining the documentation and coding standards already merged into master. Resolve the Ui documentation overlap by keeping the complete JavaDoc and the new matching-task display method.

Add Gradle Checkstyle tasks and SE-EDU-aligned rules for production and test sources.

Correct reported indentation and test-formatting violations so the new checks pass without changing application behavior.

Add a JavaFX task assistant with a separate Launcher entry point and a reusable conversation transcript. Route Ui output through a consumer so the GUI and command-line interface share the existing parser and command behavior.\n\nDocument GUI startup and add focused tests for the new output adapter. Provide a fit-for-purpose graphical interface while preserving the command-line entry point used by regression tests.

Use a boolean-sounding name for task completion state and distinguish command arguments from complete commands. Apply the same argument naming to deadline and event handlers for consistent, clearer code.
Document assumptions about UI input and parser results so programming errors are detected early.
Add assertions to command loop

Centralize task-number parsing and range validation in the base command so mark and delete commands share one implementation. This removes duplicated validation logic and keeps their user-facing errors consistent while preserving the existing behavior. Add focused tests for missing, non-numeric, and out-of-range task numbers.

Construct each saved task directly from the storage-type switch expression. This removes the mutable temporary task and statement-switch breaks, making the deserialization flow easier to read while preserving validation and status restoration behavior.

Resolve saved task markers through TaskType instead of duplicating T, D, and E literals in TaskStorage. This keeps storage parsing aligned with the enum that owns the markers and makes the supported task types explicit. Test successful and rejected marker conversions.
Branch A-CodeQuality

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams to find matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command filters tasks by description without modifying the original list.

Use a stream pipeline to express this filtering logic more directly and keep the result order unchanged.
branch-A-Streams
